name: Cloud-resident KuzuDB projection + gateway traversal -- the projection is compiled in the cloud as a consumer of the branch-head marker, served from a small always-on service on the existing opal-globgrph cluster, reached through the gateway as a thin proxy; the local copy and the local full/inc rebuild commands retire
description: Andrew-direct at the CTO~A terminal, 2026-09-02, three verbatims recorded in org/tier1_exec/1.0.0_SA_CTO~A/deliverables/ENDPOINT_FORWARD_GLOBGRPH_CLOUD_COMPILE_20260902.md: (1) ~17:5xZ 'I agree with all of these only have one comment. First, I want to clarify that this is the kuzudb projection, and that every time you reference the "graph", that is what you are referring to. Secondly, I want to clarify the stitching/incremental refresh mechanism. For the Nessie/Iceberg graph, we have an SQS queue and associated lambda that manages the stitching, however, I want to understand how we manage this on the KuzuDB basis, if it can simply be downstream of this, which I think would be a simplified architecture. Let's discuss.' (2) ~18:3xZ, in reply to /open-calls: 'I agree with all your recs. Just need to understnad the freshguard alarm and where it is interfacing as referenced in call 3.' The originating prompt (brief header, 2026-09-01): 'I'm starting to think the compilation should be done at the same time as nessie refreshes in the early morning, and the whole kuzudb and stitching is accessed in the cloud and agents who want to traverse it just traverse the cloud representation ... We want that process very abstracted away from the user so they dont have to deal with refreshing/stitching at all.' + 'yeah if thats not a runtime graph or has no automated process that is a risk surface.' THE PROJECT: the producer side of the estate graph is already cloud-resident and scheduled (nightly derive, incremental Lambda, stitch, three producers, all ending at ONE branch-head marker); the one local thing is the 47 MB KuzuDB projection, unscheduled and demand-driven (substrate card @5da9e7fffc). This project makes the projection a consumer of the marker write (S3 event -> SQS -> worker running the existing kuzu_incremental_refresh engine -> versioned artifact + pointer on S3), stands up a serving plane on the existing ECS cluster with the gateway as thin proxy, and RETIRES the local copy (PORT WITH A RETIREMENT, never coexistence). Eight ratified capability outcomes FWD-1..FWD-8 in the PRD's ENDPOINT section; coverage is explicitly NOT an outcome (brief F12). Supersedes NFRA_KUZUSPLIT O-4/P4 (never specifically ruled).
